author: Mark Schroers, Alexander Weber

title: US Plans Peace Corps Revamp to Gain Edge in AI Race With China

description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is set to mark the opening of a new parliamentary session by presenting a broad economic vision in which government policies help stoke private investment into key industries to secure the nation’s future.

description: President Donald Trump declares victory in the fight over cost-of-living concerns during a visit to Rome, Georgia. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump on Affordability: 'We've Solved It'

description: Andra Gillespie, professor at Emory University, said that President Trump has a 'big task' ahead of him to convince Americans that he has a handle on affordability, ahead of the president's speech in Rome, Georgia later today. Gillespie touched on election integrity in Georgia, after the DOJ seized voting documents related to the 2020 election. Gillespie said that the ongoing disputes around Georgia's elections have the potential to divide republicans in the state.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Takes Affordability Tour to Georgia as Americans Still Feel Squeezed

description: Meghan O'Sullivan, former deputy national security advisor in the Bush Administration, said that the buildup of military force the Trump administration has amassed in the middle east raises questions about what kind of action the US may be preparing against Iran. O'Sullivan said that there is a real possibility that US action against Iran may be 'larger, more uncertain and less contained' than previous strikes.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Warns Iran 'Really Bad Things' Will Happen Without Deal

author: Jeff Mason
description: President Donald Trump declared victory in the fight over cost-of-living concerns, signaling a new approach that sought to deny problems with his economic agenda and touting successes in job growth and other metrics.
title: Trump Says He ‘Won’ on Affordability, Signaling Messaging Shift

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss Figma's latest earnings results with CEO Dylan Field as the platform sees revenue top estimates and issues a strong growth outlook that eases broader AI fears. Then, Bloomberg News Leveraged Finance Reporter Olivia Fishlow has the latest on Blue Owl as the alternative asset manager announces a decision to restrict withdrawals from one of its private credit funds. Plus, Wayfair CFO Kate Gulliver joins to discuss the company's earnings results as shares fall Thursday on first quarter guidance, even as the online furniture retailer looks to expand its physical store footprint and lure rewards program members. Finally, Boston Children’s Hospital Chief Medical Officer Dr. Joan LaRovere joins to discuss US health policy, AI use cases and training in hospitals, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Figma's AI Outlook, Blue Owl Stokes Credit Concerns | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 2/19/2026

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss President Trump's Board of Peace meeting today in DC. On today's show, former Deputy National Security Adviser Meghan O'Sullivan, Bluestack Strategies Founder Maura Gillespie, Maywood Strategies Principal Doug Farrar and Emory University Professor Andra Gillespie. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Threatens Iran on Talks | Balance of Power: Early Edition 2/19/2026

description: Pierre Yared, acting chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, expresses cautious optimism about sustaining economic growth into 2026 and addresses recent studies claiming that over 90% of tariff costs are passed on to consumers, explaining that these pass-through regressions only measure changes in relative prices and do not identify who ultimately bears the tariff burden. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Yared Optimistic About US Growth, Weighs In on Tariff Study

description: RFK Jr. has done the opposite of what he promised in many cases — and devastated public health in the process, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Lisa Jarvis says. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Morgan Stanley’s annual “State of the States” webinar is usually a pretty staid tour of state balance sheets. This year, though, it drew more than double the usual audience and more than six times typical registration as financial advisers clamored for a chance to ask questions about what President Donald Trump’s agenda means for municipal budgets — and the bonds tied to them.

description:
The arrest of the former Prince Andrew has thrown the British royal family into uncharted waters.

The brother of King Charles has been arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office after further details emerged of his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein.

Mishal Husain explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

description:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the brother of the UK’s King Charles, has been arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office after further details of his relationship with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein emerged.
Thames Valley Police confirmed that the force had opened an investigation into an offense of misconduct in public office, and had arrested a man in his sixties. Mountbatten-Windsor turned 66 on Thursday. Bloomberg's Mishal Husain joins to discuss with Paul Sweeney and Tom Keene. (Source: Bloomberg)

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, oil has steadied following its biggest daily gain since October, following a report that American military intervention in Iran could come sooner than expected. 

OpenAI is close to finalizing a funding round topping $100 billion, led by investors including Amazon, SoftBank, Nvidia and Microsoft.

On the earnings front: Airbus says the lack of reliable engine supplies for its A320 family of jets is holding back aircraft deliveries. Meanwhile, Nestlé’s revenue will rise between 3% and 4% on an organic basis in 2026, compared with the 3.2% estimate.

Today's guests: Renault CEO François Provost & Aegon CEO Lard Friese. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran-US Conflict Concerns & OpenAI Funding Could Top $100b | Daybreak Europe 02/19/2026

description: While both the US and Iran have sounded cautiously upbeat about the latest round of diplomatic talks between the nations, analysts believe that strikes on Iranian targets remain a likely possibility.
